lines: Two real, independent pages name both of these exact ideas directly, in their own words.
One names the one place a rule like this gets written down for an entire project. The other names exactly what a real test is actually doing when it runs.
steps.takeaway: A format check, a denied rule, and a real test each catch a different mistake the other two let through.

lines: So here's what this topic's own three real checks are really standing in for: none of them is a stand in for either of the other two, because each one is actually looking at something completely different.
A format check only ever looks at how the code is laid out on the page.
A rule denied once only ever looks for one specific, named mistake it already knows about.
And a real test is the only one of the three that ever actually looks at whether the code does the right thing.
Skip any one of them, and that's exactly the kind of mistake that gets through.
